answer: Seats are earned by operating a radio relay on a surveyed ridge, not by holding keys. Each steward takes one hop between a meadow trailhead and a summit hut, and every epoch must forward a signed whisper packet reaching the next station within ninety seconds, countersigned by the hut keeper. A thousand clones on one machine share the same hop, so their signatures collapse onto one route-map segment and pay a single seat, while forged timestamps fail the hut ledger. Each hop costs a licensed site, power and a keeper, so farming identities costs more than the fixed per-seat emission.
